llm.summary: The skill largely matches its stated purpose (calling Tencent Cloud's video-effects APIs) but the package metadata omits required credentials and the runtime auto-installs packages and instructs the agent to run without asking the user — these inconsistencies increase risk.

dimensions.detail: The name/description and the code align: the script calls Tencent Cloud VCLM APIs to submit/describe a template-to-video job. However, the registry metadata declares no required environment variables or primary credential while both SKILL.md and scripts clearly require Tencent Cloud API credentials (TENCENTCLOUD_SECRET_ID, TENCENTCLOUD_SECRET_KEY, optional TENCENTCLOUD_TOKEN). That mismatch between metadata and actual requirements is an incoherence worth flagging.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to automatically execute the provided script when a user supplies an image and not to ask for confirmation ('zero-interaction principle'). The runtime instructions otherwise stay within the stated purpose (calling the cloud API, polling job state, returning the result). The agent will read local image files if a local path is supplied and will base64-encode and upload them — this file access is expected for the feature but should be noted.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no declared install spec, but scripts/main.py will auto-install the 'tencentcloud-sdk-python' package at runtime via subprocess.check_call(pip). Auto-installing packages at runtime is common but increases risk (running code fetched from PyPI at execution time). The package source is standard PyPI (not a suspicious URL), so this is moderate risk rather than a clear red flag.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The script requires Tencent Cloud credentials (TENCENTCLOUD_SECRET_ID and TENCENTCLOUD_SECRET_KEY, optional TENCENTCLOUD_TOKEN) to authenticate to vclm.tencentcloudapi.com. Those secrets are proportional to the task, but the registry metadata does not declare them — a mismatch that could lead users to provide credentials unexpectedly. No other unrelated secrets are requested.

dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true, does not claim persistence or modify other skills, and uses normal SDK calls. A notable point: SKILL.md's 'zero-interaction' rule encourages autonomous execution; combined with the undeclared credential requirement this increases the surface area but does not by itself indicate excessive platform-level privileges.

llm.guidance: This skill appears to implement the advertised Tencent Cloud video-effects flow, but before installing consider: (1) the skill's metadata does NOT declare required credentials even though the script requires TENCENTCLOUD_SECRET_ID and TENCENTCLOUD_SECRET_KEY — expect to provide API keys; (2) the script will auto-install the Tencent Cloud Python SDK via pip at runtime (code from PyPI will be executed), so run in a trusted or isolated environment if you are uncomfortable; (3) the agent is instructed to run the script automatically without asking the user — if you want explicit confirmation before uploads/execution, do not enable autonomous invocation or modify the SKILL.md behavior; (4) local image files you provide will be read and uploaded (base64-encoded) to Tencent Cloud — do not supply sensitive images or use least-privilege credentials; (5) the skill owner & homepage are unknown — if possible, verify the author or run the script manually to inspect behavior before giving credentials. If you decide to use it, provide a service account with minimal permissions and consider rotating keys after testing.
